rules.text: If the pie-slice inscriptions are the dashboard's intended market-share values for the region named in the chart title, and “current market leader” means the brand with the largest displayed market-share value, then the brand whose displayed percentage exceeds every other displayed brand percentage is the option to select for follow-up.
rules.conditions: This bridge relies on the printed slice labels accurately encoding comparable current smartphone market shares for Europe and on the task using displayed market-share leadership as its criterion.

evidence.content: The title visibly reads “Smartphone Market Share in Europe”.

evidence.location: large pale-yellow sector on the right side of the pie
red sector at lower left of the pie
orange sector at left of the pie
light-orange sector near the top of the pie

evidence.content: Review the Europe smartphone market share dashboard, then select the smartphone brand that should be marked for market-leader follow-up.
Select Samsung as the current market leader

O.reason: The supplied observations accurately transcribe visible chart inscriptions and the task evidence accurately identifies the Europe market-leader follow-up objective and Samsung option.

B.reason: The task calls for a “current market leader” but does not explicitly define that term as the brand with the largest displayed market-share percentage, nor does the image independently validate that the printed percentages are accurate comparable current shares. Rule r1 appropriately states these as conditions, but their applicability remains unverified.

implication.reason: The inscriptions visibly provide a conditional numerical basis for Samsung being the largest displayed percentage, but the conclusion and option selection depend on the unresolved r1 conditions concerning chart encoding and the task meaning of “market leader.”

This support depends on the slice inscriptions being valid and comparable market-share encodings; the image itself does not independently verify the underlying data.

refinements.condition_note: This is visual geometric corroboration only; it assumes the sectors are intended to encode the same market-share quantities represented by their inscriptions.
